conclusion: Failure-triggered rollback and resampling is not an unexplored mechanism. Existing progress-based point selection in FrozenLake may be a testable narrow variant, but novelty is not established. FrozenLake scorer uses privileged BFS environment distances; do not describe it as a general learned process scorer.

primary_sources.name: BranPO
primary_sources.finding: For hard tasks or incorrect trajectories, progressively moves truncation point backward from the last reasoning step and resamples until contrast or budget exhaustion. Also uses branch-specific advantages and redundant-step masking. Closest overlap with proposed failure-backtracking.

primary_sources.name: ReTRAIL
primary_sources.finding: Supports failure-triggered recovery and selected earlier checkpoints, preserving reflection memory. Uses state-anchored GRPO and branch-advancement reward. Overlaps trigger and restoration, differs in selection, memory and objective.

primary_sources.name: SPROUT
primary_sources.finding: Uses verifier evidence after failed attempts to plan parent and restore boundary. Shared actor analyzes/selects branches, then continues in restored execution context. Broad failure-triggered branch-point selection already studied.

primary_sources.name: LEAFE
primary_sources.finding: Reflective experience generation restores earlier decision points and branches revised actions; then supervised distillation. Related rollback mechanism, different training objective.

next_design: Compare fixed-leaf-budget existingPaTR, random rewind and progress rewind first; closest-prior late-step/backwards selector is a necessary subsequent ablation before novelty claims. Record actual tokens/actions, not just maximum leaves. No proof of literature absence from a keyword search.
